name: primitives-texts-rolling

frames.best_why: Both lines are fully settled and legible; earlier frames catch characters mid-flip.

tagline: Every letter tips up on a hinge and lands in place, one after another.
summary: Two lines of text that arrive as individual characters flipping around a horizontal axis, sweeping left to right, the subtitle starting after a short pause.
appearance: A large bold white headline and a smaller grey subtitle, both centred on a near-black stage. During the effect a character is briefly edge-on or missing, leaving a gap in the line until it drops back into place.
behaviour: On entering the viewport each character rotates ninety degrees up into its slot, staggered along the sentence; the second line waits a little longer. Everything settles into still, normally spaced text.
demo_content: "Welcome to Animate UI" over "Beautiful animations made easy"
search_phrases: letters flip into place one by one
text rolls in character by character
headline flips up on scroll into view
use_when: A hero headline should arrive with a rewarding reveal once it scrolls into view.
avoid_when: Body copy or long paragraphs: per-character delays slow reading and the motion distracts.
customise: Text, an extra delay and the transition timing come in as props; changing the flip axis or the per-character stagger needs a source edit.
weight_why: A few spans per character driven by two transforms each, with no running loop.

a11y.note: The visible characters are hidden from assistive tech and the full text is exposed, but there is no reduced-motion fallback.

polish_why: Crisp staggered flip with sensible timing; the grey subtitle sits low in contrast on black.
